cut_items.item: Only retry on network errors, 5xx and 429; don't retry card declines or other 4xx errors
Double-clicking Pay or page refresh can cause the same duplicate; deriving the key from order ID covers it
Explicit step-by-step failure sequence (request sent, charged, response lost, retry creates a second charge)
Using a fresh UUID inside the retry loop protects nothing
Offer to inspect the checkout code to check where the key is created
PaymentIntents also handles 3D Secure better and idempotency keys work the same there
Only retry on network errors, 5xx and 429; do not retry card declines or other 4xx
Double-click or refresh on Pay can cause duplicates; deriving the key from the order ID covers it
PaymentIntents handles retries and 3D Secure better, and idempotency keys work the same way there
Offer to inspect the checkout code to verify where the key is created

added_items.item: Persist the key before the first call so a crash and restart reuses the same key
Reusing one key across different orders returns the first customer's result to the second customer
Search Stripe for existing duplicate charges (same customer, amount, order metadata within a short time) to audit past retries
stripe-node usage: pass { idempotencyKey } as a request option
Retry must reuse the exact same parameters as well as the same key
Check your SDK version before relying on maxNetworkRetries auto-keys
Retry within the 24-hour key window since keys may be removed after that
